order_note: This document is committed BEFORE any performance attempt of the roles below. Stop rules and expected failure modes are declared here and cannot be revised after observing results.
environment: SUBJECT-FREEZE.json (same runtime/model/prompt/reference for every role; only placement shape varies)
subject: AMD-A (Vulkan1 / 02:00.0); NV-A (Vulkan3 / 04:00.0) participates as the matched peer device with identical link class

roles.intent: KNOWN ADVERSE CASE: reproduce the communication-sensitive failure mode. Under current supported semantics the finest-grained supported multiworker shape is a full layer split across two x1 links (row/tensor split is rejected by the runtime on these backends: 'does not support split buffers' — retained as expected-failure control R0). Every generated token crosses the split boundary on both x1 links. AMENDED pre-execution: executes as -sm layer (row-split builder retained only for control R0).
roles.stop_rules: run all attempts; classify from medians; no early stop on a fast or slow first attempt

roles.intent: CONTROL R0: prove the row-split (tensor) path is unsupported on these backends under the frozen runtime; expected to fail closed at model load. Retained to show the sweep did not silently fall back from the intended finer-grained shape.
roles.expected_failure_mode: runtime model-load failure: split buffers unsupported on these Vulkan backends
roles.stop_rules: single attempt; any non-zero exit with the load error retained as EXPECTED_FAILURE

roles.intent: COARSER EXECUTION UNIT: contiguous layer blocks per device (pipeline shape); boundary traffic per token only at graph splits. Compare against the single-subject control to measure the marginal throughput effect of adding the second x1 participant. NOTE: with both devices fully offloaded the runtime assigns contiguous layer ranges; the split point is the runtime's, not ours. AMENDED pre-execution: coarser unit = batch -np 4 (only supported coarser-execution-unit knob); correctness recorded as clean-exit/complete-offload/raw-retention, not byte-exact vs the single-sequence reference.
roles.stop_rules: run all attempts; classify from medians

roles.intent: MATCHED CONTROL: AMD-A alone, all layers resident, zero cross-link traffic per token. The matched baseline for marginal effects of every multiworker role.
roles.stop_rules: run all attempts; classify from medians

roles.intent: MATCHED CONTROL (cross-device arm): NV-A alone under the identical workload; separates device-local compute differences from link-class effects (both subjects share the x1 link class).
roles.stop_rules: run all attempts; classify from medians

roles.intent: CAPACITY-FEASIBILITY CASE: a model (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct Q4_K_M, ~4.4 GiB weights, >8 GiB with KV+compute) that cannot execute fully resident on ONE subject (8 GiB VRAM each) is executed with BOTH x1 subjects participating under layer split. Feasibility/completeness is the measured fact; throughput is recorded but NOT compared as a race against an impossible single-subject baseline (the matched control is partial-offload single-subject, recorded for honesty).
roles.model_override: /home/zutfen/.cache/v0c-models/i35/qwen2.5-14b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf (concatenated multi-part GGUF, digest recorded at execution)
roles.stop_rules: clean exit + complete offload = capacity-feasible; any load failure = NOT_FEASIBLE_ON_TESTED_SUBSTRATE, retained

roles.intent: MATCHED CONTROL for the capacity case: the SAME 14B model on ONE subject with the runtime's own memory fitting (auto-reduced offload). Establishes the honest single-subject comparison point (partial offload, host paging) so the capacity case's marginal effect is measured, not asserted.
roles.stop_rules: record offload fraction and throughput whatever they are; a clean exit with partial offload is the expected honest outcome

excluded_shapes.reason: EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT under current supported semantics: the frozen runtime exposes no genuinely less-frequently-used execution unit for this workload class; synthesizing sparse demand is forbidden by the issue
runtime rejects split buffers on both backends (control R0 retained); NOT silently replaced by approximations
NOT_PHYSICALLY_AVAILABLE: all root ports on this host are electrically x1; no hardware moves are in scope

cross_device_note: AMD-A and NV-A share the measured x1 link class (both Gen1-class under load on this substrate). The single-subject controls separate device-local compute; multiworker roles with the same peer shape across both subjects separate link-dominated from device-dominated effects.

pre_execution_amendment.note: Amended BEFORE any role-sweep execution attempt (transport substrate measurement only had run). Two mechanical reconciliations with verified runtime behavior, neither selected after observing role performance:
changes: adverse role: the row-split builder is retained ONLY for the unsupported-shape control R0; the adverse role itself executes as the layer split (-sm layer), which its committed intent already declares is the finest supported multiworker shape ('full layer split across two x1 links; every generated token crosses the split boundary')

coarse role: distinguished from adverse by the only supported coarser-execution-unit knob: batch parallelism -np 4 (4 sequences per decode step amortize the same per-token boundary transfer over 4x useful work; same model, same greedy per-sequence semantics). Because the visible output of a 4-sequence batch is not byte-comparable to the single-sequence frozen reference, the coarse role records correctness as clean-exit + complete-offload + raw retention, not byte-exact comparison; the freeze's correctness_reference entry for this role is accordingly dropped
